one_line_summary: An independent PyTorch confusion-scheme rerun on the authors’ η=0.02 Zenodo configurations reproduces the W-shape and the ≈−1050 transition peak, but the ≈−900 transition is shifted to ≈−930 and some paper settings/etas were not replicated.
reasoning: The replication actually executed the confusion workflow on the published equilibrium configurations and recovered the hallmark W-shaped accuracy curve, supporting C1. It matches the paper’s η=0.02 low-energy transition near E≈−1050 extremely well (≈−1048), but the higher-energy transition appears nearer ≈−930 (and/or ≈−972) rather than ≈−900, yielding only partial numerical agreement for C2. Claims for η=0.06 (C3) and the “no tuning needed” sufficiency under the paper’s full sampling/restarts (C4) were not fully tested due to reduced restarts/configurations and only one η value.
strong_points: Used the authors’ released Zenodo configurations (real data) and an independently written PyTorch implementation (not derived from the authors’ code).
Recovered a clear W-shape with strong peak–valley contrast and small reported variability, consistent with the confusion-scheme signature (supports C1).
Excellent quantitative agreement for the key η=0.02 transition at ≈−1050 (found ≈−1048.1), strengthening confidence in the main low-energy transition (supports C2 in part).
Performed both narrow and wider sweeps and correctly noted edge-truncation effects on peak detectability.
caveats: Only η=0.02 was tested; η=0.06 three-transition claim (C3) remains unverified.
Training budget differs materially from the paper (5 vs 10 restarts; 500 vs 2000 configs/bin), which could shift/merge peaks and affects the strength of conclusions about C4.

The higher-energy transition location disagrees by ~30 energy units (paper ≈−900 vs replication ≈−930, with another peak at ≈−972), so the open-chain→loop transition is not cleanly reproduced numerically.
The wide sweep was partial (terminated at bin 41), and the narrow sweep initially truncated the left flank of the ≈−1050 peak, limiting full-shape characterization in that run.
